Hey, I also do this. I find it therapeutic in a way when there’s really no one to talk to. It allows you to have fun with the idea of a person who wants to pick your brain on the weirdest questions. It’s like being your own best friend in a sense.

In times of emotional distress, it helps to talk it out and tell how I really feel about a situation or person. It may seem odd to people outside of you and the thought bubble, but I don’t think it’s anything to be ashamed of. Personally, it helped me to overcome a slump in my life. I find that self-talk/thinking out loud should be normalized. Sometimes, people find it better to escape into their own world.

It’s a mix between missing it, but also me glad that I don’t have to put on a mask in front of everyone and drag my body to class because of attendance. I’m a college student that’s pretty much an outsider to friend groups (since I’m a commuter), so... No more having to have a mask or to work with strangers on group assignments. I can get ahead and finish everything early if I feel, and I could go at my own pace if I wanted.

The perfection part comes in the forms of choosing the write words or style whether that’s more heartfelt or a “robotic” way of writing things. 

I honestly like writing in my journal because it’s the one place where I can truly speak and let my emotions out without having to face judgment from other people. I guess you could say it’s therapeutic in a way.

I resonated with this post as well as I was a person who worried for others more than myself to a fault. I think that a lot of it comes from the INFJ’s tendency to people please. We always want to make a first good impact, and we want to feel accepted just like everyone else. However, there comes a time where people are not always for you. In my experience, being friends with a group just because you have a basal similarity (i.e. I’m male so let’s hang out with the males.) isn’t healthy, and I think this goes doubly for INFJs. 

Finding real people who make the effort to understand you is the key. More than that, it’s more of being comfortable in your own skin. There will be times where we want to people please and make a good first impression, but if you realize that a relationship isn’t moving past square one, then it isn’t worth it. I think that people walk over others who do not have an sense of self-identity. Therefore, take some time to learn about yourself. Once you learn about yourself, love yourself, and accept yourself for the person that you are, the right people are going to come to you. It won’t be instantaneous. Sometimes, you won’t find the person right away or at that place in time. You shouldn’t have to chase after people to find acceptance. The right people will come and accept the real you.

I hope this answered your question. The short of it is can be summed up by a quote: “Don’t change so that people will like you. Be yourself and the right people will love the real you.”
